subject: Convergent MAP: tokens-per-$ signoff & evaluation timeline
messages:
From: kimberly.park@redwood.inference
To: ben.carter@redwood.inference, david.kim@redwood.inference, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference, sara.lee@nexahealth.com
Cc: procurement@nexahealth.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Convergent MAP: tokens-per-$ signoff & evaluation timeline

Team / Sara —

I pulled together a focused MAP appendix that isolates the token economics items we discussed in the demo: tokens/$ baseline, KV cache hit-rate assumptions, batching profile, and burst capacity costs. Attached are two artifacts: a working MAP spreadsheet (Nexa_MAP_v3.xlsx) and the simulation output (token-econ-run-sim.csv).

High-level asks:
- Ben / David: can you confirm whether our 95% KV hit-rate assumption is realistic for Nexa's conversational flow, or if we should scope to 85% for MAP signoff?
- Tessa: can you sanity-check the batching assumptions (avg batch window 60ms, 10 requests/batch) vs. Dedicated capacity billing?
- Sara / Procurement: would you accept a MAP signoff that conditions pricing on the simulation results (i.e., final tokens/$ locked after pilot pass)?

Timing: ideally we want MAP signoff before procurement starts redlines. Proposed timeline in sheet is: run sims Friday 5/21 -> internal signoff 5/22 -> procurement review week of 5/25. If anything blocks that, call it out.

I flagged a few cells in the spreadsheet with open assumptions and added a short comments tab. Short replies are fine — I want to consolidate changes then circulate the next MAP revision.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Nexa_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), token-econ-run-sim.csv (csv)

From: ben.carter@redwood.inference
To: kimberly.park@redwood.inference, david.kim@redwood.inference, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference, sara.lee@nexahealth.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Convergent MAP: tokens-per-$ signoff & evaluation timeline

Kim / all —

Quick pass from infra/ops perspective after scanning token-econ-run-sim.csv:
- KV cache: our historical pilots average ~88% hit-rate for short-conversation flows (<6 turns). 95% is optimistic unless Nexa prefetches or pins prefixes. Recommend we budget 85% in MAP and note 95% as stretch with guidance on prefetching.
- Batching: 10 requests/batch and 60ms window is reasonable for morning traffic but will underperform during spikes. Suggest we include a fallback plan that drops batching aggressiveness below 30ms when p95 latency > 220ms.
- Per-token cost delta: with 85% KV hit-rate we're seeing ~12-15% higher tokens/$ than the sheet's baseline. See attached short note: token-econ-ops-notes.pdf.

I'll update the sim with the 85% run and send by EOD. If Nexa needs conservative pricing for procurement, we can include an acceptance gate in the MAP that allows a single post-pilot re-quote based on measured hit-rate.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: token-econ-ops-notes.pdf

From: david.kim@redwood.inference
To: kimberly.park@redwood.inference, ben.carter@redwood.inference, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference, sara.lee@nexahealth.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Convergent MAP: tokens-per-$ signoff & evaluation timeline

On Wed, May 20, 2026 at 10:04 AM ben.carter@redwood.inference wrote:
> KV cache: our historical pilots average ~88% hit-rate for short-conversation flows (<6 turns). 95% is optimistic...

All — good notes. From procurement/billing lens: Nexa's legal team asked for a clear trigger for any price adjustment post-pilot. I propose we add the following MAP clauses:

1) Acceptance gate: pilot period = 30 days, sample window = 72 hours during week 2 of pilot. If measured KV hit-rate >= 90% and avg tokens/$ <= baseline + 8%, price locked.
2) Re-quote clause: if measured KV hit-rate < 90%, Redwood will provide a revised unit price within 5 business days. Customer may accept revised price or continue at pilot rates until an agreed ramp date.
3) Burst capacity surcharge: add a listed surcharge formula when sustained burst capacity > 3x baseline for >10 minutes (explicit example in spreadsheet).

Proposed MAP timeline (ref: Drive):
- 5/21 EOD: Ben uploads 85% sim; Kimberly collates changes
- 5/22 11:00 AM PT: internal signoff call (sales + ops + procurement)
- 5/22 EOD: send final MAP v3 to Nexa procurement for review
- 5/25: Nexa legal redlines due

If Nexa is comfortable, we can lock the MAP and routing of procurement next week. HubSpot deal NX-9231 updated with attachments: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/NX-9231 (internal ref).

-David Kim
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@nexahealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.inference, ben.carter@redwood.inference, david.kim@redwood.inference, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference
Date: Sat, 22 May 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Convergent MAP: tokens-per-$ signoff & evaluation timeline

Kim / team —

Thanks for the thorough breakdown and the draft MAP spreadsheet. Procurement appreciates the explicit acceptance gate and the re-quote timeline — that gives us the structure we need for our finance review. A couple of quick clarifications before we circulate to legal: 

- Can you add a worked example row in the spreadsheet that shows the cost delta for a 60% vs 90% KV hit-rate with a 3x burst event? That visual will speed our CFO's review.
- For the burst surcharge, can you confirm whether the surcharge is applied per-minute or per-event? We prefer per-event but can accept per-minute if the formula caps exposure (please add a cap example).

If you can get an updated XLSX with the example row and a capped surcharge example by Monday morning (5/24), we'll aim to have legal start redlines on 5/25. Otherwise this timeline slips a week.

Sara Lee
Sr. Director, Product Ops
Nexa Health

P.S. We downloaded Nexa_MAP_v3.xlsx and noted the comments tab. Please label any new examples "Finance Example" so our CFO's team can find them quickly.
